query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Cryo-rolling and annealing can be used for concurrent strength-ductility improvement in high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Nano-Lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 Eutectic High Entropy Alloy
generation.conditions: Multi-pass cryo-rolling up to ~90% reduction in thickness with immersion in liquid N2 for 45 minutes before and after each pass, followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 hour and water quenching
generation.structural_mediator: Hierarchical microstructure consisting of fine lamellar regions with ultrafine FCC grains and coarse non-lamellar regions with coarse unrecrystallized B2 phase
generation.mechanism: Back-stress hardening effect and dislocation multiplication and tangle
generation.predicted_outcome: Simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility
generation.baseline: As-cast material with Yield Strength (YS) of ~1000 MPa and Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) of ~1200 MPa, and elongation to failure (ef) of ~17%
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms and optimal processing conditions for concurrent strength-ductility improvement are still unclear

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the cryo-rolled and annealed material does not exhibit simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How can cryo-rolling and annealing be utilized to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in multiphase high entropy alloys, specifically regarding the development of a hierarchical microstructure?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA). Processing: Multi-pass cryo-rolling up to ~90% reduction in thickness with immersion in liquid N2 for 45 minutes before and after each pass, followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 hour and water quenching.. Test conditions: Tensile tests at ambient temperature with an initial strain rate of 8.3 × 10−4 s−1; Nano-indentation with load increased linearly from 1 μN to 500 μN over 0.25 seconds..
